issues.problem: Fence recognition only accepts delimiters preceded by up to three spaces. Valid CommonMark fences starting on a list-marker line (e.g. '- ```md') are not recognized, so indented headings inside them are counted and the closing fence may be mistaken for a new opening fence.
issues.suggested_fix: Track list-container prefixes when recognizing fenced blocks, or use a small container-aware fence scanner. Add regression tests for bullet and numbered-list fences asserting fenced headings are excluded and headings after the fence remain visible.
issues.failure_scenario: For '- ```md / ## Phantom / ``` / ## Real', headingKeys() returns Phantom and loses Real. A component named Phantom makes pack.expo.docs falsely PASS, while a genuinely documented Real component is reported missing.
issues.evidence:
entries.mjs:101 FENCE=/^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})/ and opens() at :108 never see a fence after a list marker. Ran headingKeys on '- ```md
## Phantom
```
## Real' and got ['Phantom']: Real is lost, because the closing ``` is read as a new opening fence. The indented form '- ```md
  ## Phantom
  ```
## Real' gives the same result. The defect holds. One detail of the scenario is imprecise: in the column-0 form CommonMark ends the list item, so Phantom is a real heading there. The Phantom-counted-falsely claim is only true for properly indented content. Losing Real is wrong either way.

issues.problem: The advice says any later block that sets such a rule's options makes the rule overridden. The engine accepts an effective entry whose options equal the pack's options; only differing options cause rejection.
issues.suggested_fix: Say 'sets different options' or state that the resulting effective configuration determines whether the rule is measured. Add a wording/behavior test covering an identical-options later block.
issues.failure_scenario: An app already configures max-lines-per-function with exactly the pack's severity and options. Spreading the pack before that block remains measured, but setup tells the developer it will be unmeasured and may prompt an unnecessary placement decision.
issues.evidence: packages/cookwright/src/lib/packs/standards.mjs:101,107-109: judge() returns MEASURED when severity is error and subset(want, options[0]) holds, i.e. each key of the pack's options deep-equals the effective entry's. A later block with identical options (or a superset) stays measured. Only differing options give 'overridden'. messages.mjs:39-40 (and the comment at :33-35) say a block 'that sets such a rule's options' leaves it overridden. The same wording is in docs/guides/standards.md:23 and skills/setup/SKILL.md:164, with no 'differing' qualifier. So the advice overstates, and setup can prompt for a placement decision that makes no difference. Severity is P3.

issues.location: line 164, the pack.expo.lint / pack.supabase.lint '… does not name …' remedy (commit 8578782); same claim in docs/guides/standards.md line 23
issues.problem: The fix swapped reading the config file's own blocks for running `npx eslint --print-config` on two sample files: a .tsx under the components directory and a .ts file. The file's own blocks are now read only when ESLint does not run. --print-config only returns the blocks whose `files` match the sampled path. The pack's rules reach much further: strings covers every **/*.{tsx,jsx}, size covers **/*.{ts,js} and **/*.{tsx,jsx}, and the supabase client rule covers every **/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx} outside the service paths. So an app block scoped to a directory or extension the samples miss is never seen. The previous wording read the file and caught it. This is a regression the fix introduced. The guide's new sentence also claims more than the skill does: it says the skill counts 'a rule a spread preset sets … as well as one your file shows', but a block the file shows is missed whenever the samples do not match it.
issues.suggested_fix: When ESLint runs, keep both checks: read the config file's own blocks for any of the four rule ids (any `files` scope), and add the --print-config results for presets. Or sample one file per pack block glob (.tsx, .jsx, .ts, .js, and one under each directory the file's blocks scope to). Then word the guide's sentence to match what is actually checked.
issues.failure_scenario: An app's eslint.config.js has `{ files: ['src/features/**/*.ts'], rules: { 'no-restricted-imports': ['error', { paths: ['lodash'] }] } }` and `{ files: ['scripts/**/*.js'], rules: { 'max-lines-per-function': ['error', { max: 200 }] } }`. The skill runs --print-config on src/components/Button.tsx and src/lib.ts. Neither matches those blocks, so neither rule id is listed. The skill concludes 'None set' and appends both pack spreads at the end of the array without asking. Flat config then replaces the app's no-restricted-imports options on src/features/** (the lodash ban is gone) and its 200-line limit on scripts/** (now 40). The pack's rules read measured, so doctor and the ratchet report nothing, and the developer never chose this. It is the harm QA Q2 and review finding 2 were meant to prevent.
issues.evidence: packages/cookwright/skills/setup/SKILL.md:164 detects set rules only from `npx eslint --print-config` on two sample files (a .tsx under components and a .ts); the file's own blocks are read only when ESLint does not run. --print-config returns only blocks whose `files` match the sampled path. The pack rules cover wider globs (packs/expo/eslint.cjs:84,108,109 `**/*.{tsx,jsx}` and `**/*.{ts,js}`; packs/supabase/eslint.cjs:22 `**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}`). A block scoped to src/features/**/*.ts or scripts/**/*.js is therefore not listed, the skill concludes 'None set', and it appends the spread last without asking, which replaces the app's options on those paths. docs/guides/standards.md:23 says a rule 'your file shows' counts, which the skill does not guarantee. The regression is real: the fix removed the file-block read from the normal path.

issues.problem: Commit 348abb4 made headingKeys follow CommonMark fences, but docKeys still merges tableKeys, which ignores fences entirely. A table row inside a fenced code block still counts as an entry. The standards guide's sentence 'An entry is a table row's first cell or a `## <key>` or `### <key>` heading (outside a fenced code block)' reads naturally as excluding fenced content of both kinds. The commit message also skipped doc-sync on the grounds that the code now matches that sentence. That holds for headings only.
issues.suggested_fix: Run the same fence tracker (opens/closes) in tableKeys so fenced table rows are skipped, and add a test. Or reword the guide so the fence exclusion clearly applies to headings only.
